text_rules: Keep cover text to 3-5 punchy words mixing Hindi + English, always include a specific number (₹ amount, GSM, piece count, or a quantity) to create concrete stakes. Use a question mark or accusatory tone to trigger curiosity — avoid generic educational labels like 'फर्क समझो' or dictionary-style definitions that feel like textbook content.
layout: Place all text in a single bold cluster within the 25%-70% vertical band (safe from Instagram grid-crop at top and YouTube UI at bottom), left-aligned or centered with the product/fabric/damage visual filling the remaining space as a background. Use yellow (#FFD400) for the key number or shocking keyword and white for the remaining words, with a thick black stroke/shadow on every letter for mobile legibility at thumbnail size.
patterns: Top-performing Indian business Reels thumbnails follow a 'money-at-risk story' formula: a specific rupee loss or piece count + a concrete failure mode (crack, peel, reject, shape loss) compressed into 3-5 words that read like a mini-headline of disaster. Winning covers never explain — they accuse or question, making the viewer feel they might be the next victim. Illustration-style or comparison-diagram covers with cream/navy palettes drastically underperform versus high-contrast yellow-white-on-dark covers with real product/warehouse imagery behind the text.
ig_patterns: Highest save-rate covers (1.7%+) promise a reusable checklist or diagnostic framework hidden behind a loss story ('200 GSM Felt Cheap — 3 Checks'), making viewers bookmark them as reference tools for future orders. Highest share-rate covers (1.7%+) describe a universally relatable supplier scam or seasonal failure (humidity, yarn swap) that triggers 'my retailer friend needs to see this' forwarding behavior. Cream/navy illustration covers and purely technical Hindi labels ('BIOWASH ≠ PRESHRUNK') consistently get near-zero saves and shares — the algorithm and audience both reject anything that looks educational without emotional stakes.
